source_packet.job_description_text: Senior Tax Associate at Northwind. Hybrid NYC. Reports to the Director of Tax. Owns multi-state sales tax compliance across our twelve production-entity LLCs. Manages quarterly partnership tax provisions and annual K-1 distribution. Partners with finance leadership on close coordination, especially during production wrap. Avalara experience preferred but not required. CPA required. Six-plus years of public accounting plus in-house experience strongly preferred. The hire is meant to take sales tax fully off the Director's plate within the first year so she can focus on entity-structure work.

content: Got the JD. Couple things I want to confirm before I start scoping — sound good?

OK — senior tax associate, hybrid NYC, reports to the Director of Tax, owns sales tax across twelve LLCs, partnership tax provisions, K-1 distribution, partner with finance on close. CPA required, six-plus years, Avalara nice to have. The piece I want to confirm: when the JD says 'take sales tax off the Director's plate within the first year,' does that mean the new hire owns it day one and the Director just supervises, or does the new hire grow into ownership over the year?

content: Grow into it. First quarter is shadowing the Director on the existing process. By Q3 they own the close themselves.

Got it — Q1 shadow, Q3 owner. So in the first year, the bar for 'good' is they're operating the Director's existing process competently and inheriting it cleanly. Builder-grade comes later. Sound right?

depth_distinction.builder_definition: By Q3 owns the multi-state sales tax close end-to-end across the twelve production-entity LLCs. Builder is the year-two state.
depth_distinction.user_definition: Year-one bar: shadows the Director through Q1, operates the Director's existing process competently, inherits ownership through Q3.
depth_distinction.edge_case_guidance: A candidate who can't credibly take ownership by Q3 is not a fit even if year-one shadowing would go fine.

content: Yeah, exactly that. CPA is non-negotiable, and at least one of the six years has to be in-house — pure public accounting won't cut it.
CPA hard line, in-house experience required — those go into the minimum bar. Anything else like that, or is that the floor?

updates.minimum_bar_description: CPA required. At least one year of in-house experience inside the six-plus years total. Pure public-accounting profiles do not pass.
